ov: More than 200 species of mostly solitary, nocturnal birds of prey, with an upright stance, a broad head, forward-facing eyes and feathers adapted for near-silent flight.

why.ac: Most owls hunt at night, but a few, like the northern hawk-owl, are active by day.

rg: Every region of the Earth except the polar ice caps and some remote islands.
df: Mostly small mammals, insects and other birds; a few species specialise in fish. Bones and fur are coughed up as pellets.
fx: Serrated edges on its wing feathers break up the air, making its flight almost silent.
